author: Darryl Coote
title: New York AG named special prosecutor in Cornell gang-rape case - NewsBreak
text:
By Darryl Coote ,
15 minutes ago Oct. 1 (UPI) -- New York Gov. Kathy Hochul named the state's attorney general, Letitia James, on Thursday as special prosecutor to investigate allegations that a female student was drugged and gang-raped at a Cornell University fraternity house in fall 2024.
Letitia James, attorney general of New York, was named special prosecutor Thursday to investigate a woman's allegations that she was gang-raped by seven members of a Cornell University fraternity in October 2024. File Photo by Derek French/UPI Hochul named James as special prosecutor in an executive order , handing James the case from Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten, who has come under mounting criticism over his office's initial handling of the woman's allegations.
"Newly released information continues to raise serious questions about the investigation conducted by the Cornell Police Department and the decision by the Tompkins County district attorney not to prosecute an alleged sexual assault on Cornell University's campus in October 2024," Hochul said in a statement .
"This has, in turn, undercut my faith, and the public's faith, in the district attorney's ability to effectively investigate and prosecute the case at this time."
James will investigate the allegations and, if warranted, prosecute any offenses her office discovers, Hochul said.
"The young woman at the center of this case deserves to know that every fact will be examined and justice pursued," the governor said.
James responded online that her office does not take the responsibility in trusted in her by the governor lightly.
"I stand ready to lead a process guided by the facts and the law," she said in a statement .
The woman, identified in court documents as Jane Doe, alleges she was drugged and gang-raped for hours by seven members of Cornell's Chi Phi fraternity overnight Oct. 19-20, 2024.
Police were informed following the incident, but no charges were brought against any of the men allegedly involved. And though the allegations were made public in November that year, additional details only became public last month in a civil lawsuit filed by the woman seeking compensatory and punitive damages from Cornell and her alleged attackers.
Since the lawsuit was filed, the Ithaca, N.Y., Ivy League school and local law enforcement have faced mounting public anger over perceived failures to adequately respond to the woman's allegations.
Amid the backlash, Van Houten announced that he was reopening the case. He has also defended his office's initial decision to not prosecute any of the men on the grounds that the woman did not allege in her initial sworn statement "that she was drugged against her will or gang-raped."
Hochul's executive order states that Van Houten declined to prosecute without speaking to Jane Doe and relied, at lest in part, on information from her sworn statement to the Cornell University Police Department, which reportedly omitted key portions of her account, including her "unequivocal assertion that she had been sexually assaulted."
The governor naming James as special prosecutor is the latest action Hochul has taken following Jane Doe's filing of the lawsuit on Sept. 16.
She has called for an independent, third-party investigation of Cornell's response to Jane Doe's allegations, which the university on Wednesday said it has agreed to.
